children: Crude futures settle higher in a choppy session ahead of the U.S. Labor Day long weekend, closing out a week of gains that saw the resumption of U.S. strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian attacks on shipping. Oil price gains have been tempered by limited flows getting through the Strait of Hormuz, although differences remain on how much oil is making it out. A bigger-than-expected 4.5 million barrel draw in U.S. crude stocks reported midweek by the EIA added upside pressure. WTI settles up 0.2% at $91.48 a barrel, up 9.7% on the week. Brent rises 0.8% to $96.28, or 9.3% higher than a week ago.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
